title: Argand diagram & modulus–argument
examples: How do I plot a complex number on the Argand diagram?
What is the relationship between the modulus and the distance from the origin?
Can you show me an example of finding a locus using complex numbers?

explain.say: Today we look at the complex plane. This graph helps us plot complex numbers. A complex number z is written as a plus sign i times a number. We plot this using two axes.
The horizontal axis is the real axis. The vertical axis is the imaginary axis. A number like three plus two i is plotted at three across and two up.

The modulus of z, written as the capital letter R, is its distance from the origin. We find this using the square root of the sum of the squares. For three plus two i, the modulus is the square root of nine plus four.
The argument, or angle, is measured from the positive real axis. We use the tangent function to find this angle. For three plus two i, the argument is the angle whose tangent is two divided by three.
We can write z in polar form using the modulus and argument. This form is r times the cosine of theta plus i times the sine of theta. So z equals r times cosine theta plus i times sine theta.

items: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ)
Polar form using modulus and argument

draw.text: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ)

faq.q: How do I find the modulus if the number is negative?
faq.a: The modulus is always a positive distance. You use the formula square root of the real part squared plus the imaginary part squared. You can also find it by treating the coordinates as x and y.
asks: What is the distance from the origin?
How do I find the length of the complex number?

faq.q: What is the difference between argument and angle?
faq.a: The argument is the specific angle measured in radians or degrees on the complex plane. It tells you the direction of the number from the positive real axis. It is related to the angle you find using trigonometry.
asks: Is the argument the same as the angle?
How do I measure the angle of a complex number?

faq.q: When do I need to worry about the quadrant?
faq.a: You must check which quadrant the number lies in. The basic arctan function only gives angles in the first quadrant. You might need to add or subtract pi or pi radians to get the correct angle. This is very important.
asks: What if the number is in the second quadrant?

faq.q: How do I plot a locus?
faq.a: A locus is the set of all points satisfying a given condition. You usually express the condition using z and then convert it into an equation relating x and y. You then plot this equation on the complex plane.
asks: What is a locus in this context?
How do I graph a set of points?

faq.q: Is the polar form always easier to use?
faq.a: It depends on the problem. For multiplication or powers, polar form is often much simpler. However, if you are given coordinates, converting to rectangular form first might be easier. Both forms are useful tools.
asks: When should I use polar form?
Is there a time when rectangular form is better?

facts: The complex plane uses two axes: the real axis and the imaginary axis.
The modulus, or magnitude, of a complex number z = x + iy is calculated as square root of x squared plus y squared.
The argument, or angle, is typically measured in radians, although degrees can also be used.
The polar form of a complex number is r times cosine theta plus i times sine theta.

quiz.say: A complex number is plotted at the point two plus two i. What is its modulus?
quiz.why: The modulus is the distance from the origin, calculated as square root of two squared plus two squared, which is four.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you might simply add the real and imaginary parts together.
wrong.2: This might happen if you only take the smaller of the two coordinates.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you must square both the real and imaginary parts before adding them.

quiz.say: If a complex number has a modulus of five and an argument of pi over four, what is its rectangular form?
quiz.why: You use cosine and sine with the modulus: five times cosine pi over four plus i times five times sine pi over four.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you must use the trigonometric functions, not just the modulus itself.
wrong.1: This confuses the polar form with a simple multiplication of the modulus.
wrong.2: This is technically correct but not the required final rectangular form.

quiz.say: The equation |z - 1| = 3 describes what shape on the complex plane?

options.show: A circle centered at the origin.
options.say: A circle centered at the origin.

options.show: A circle centered at one, with radius three.
options.say: A circle centered at one, with radius three.

options.show: A straight line passing through one.
options.say: A straight line passing through one.

quiz.why: The form |z - z₀| = r always represents a circle centered at z₀ with radius r. Here z₀ is one and r is three.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the subtraction of one shifts the center away from the origin.
wrong.1: This would only be true if the right side of the equation was zero.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the modulus equaling a constant distance always forms a curve, not a line.
